minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard FY24 budget requests from Council on Aging, Land Use and Library; no budget votes taken.
minutes.summary: The committee opened budget season with department presentations from the Council on Aging, Land Use and the Library, asking questions on each. It then discussed the Finance Committee's Town Meeting report, the tax abatement backlog, and preparing for a March 7 meeting with state legislators. The only votes were approving minutes and adjourning.

Grant is driven by census counts at a per-elder rate; amount rose with the UMass survey count, and a lower federal count may come.
A member confirmed the total budget including the increase.
Patio funded by a state earmark that must be spent by June 30, capital plan money, and donations.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard FY24 budget requests from the Council on Aging, then Land Use, then the Library, and took no budget votes.
The Council on Aging director asked for an increase, mainly for a part-time outreach assistant and a fuller municipal share of the meal site manager's position.
The Library director said the state minimum for FY24 is well below the request and the town manager's preliminary budget, and listed requests for staff title, equipment and materials.
The committee agreed to begin outlining its Town Meeting report as a living document, with the chair and Evan collecting topics.
The chair will consider asking town officials for a most-likely schedule on tax abatement decisions, and Evan and Chris will draft questions for state legislators.

why_it_matters: These are the first FY24 department requests, and the Council on Aging and Library increases would be funded from the town budget, mostly taxes, if approved at Town Meeting.
The abatement backlog and the legislator meeting bear on how much the town can count on for revenue and how soon abatement decisions will be settled.
